section.book: Bittinger, Beecher, Ellenbogen & Penna, College Algebra: Graphs and Models, 7e
section.title: Solving Equations and Inequalities with Absolute Value

title: Solve |ax + b| > c (two pieces joined by or)
sources: OpenStax College Algebra 2e §2.7 p. 162 (CC BY 4.0): method only
process_card: Solving an absolute value inequality with greater than

problem.prompt: Solve and write the solution set in interval notation: {tex:absx} > {tex:cd}

steps.name: write two inequalities joined by or
write the union in interval notation

mistakes.name: wrote one interval (that is for less than)
mistakes.message: |X| > c means X < -c or X > c: two pieces on the outside.

mistakes.name: wrong bracket type
mistakes.message: < and > leave the endpoints out: ( ). ≤ and ≥ include them: [ ].

hints.hint: Add the number subtracted outside the bars to both sides.
hints.why: The rule works only on |X| compared with c.

hints.step: write two inequalities joined by or
hints.hint: X below -c, or X above c.
hints.why: More than c units from 0 is out on either side.

hints.hint: Dividing by a negative reverses the sign.
hints.why: Multiplying by a negative flips the order on the number line.

hints.step: write the union in interval notation
hints.hint: Left piece ∪ right piece; parenthesis at infinity.
